name: East Face (2002)

pitch_detail.notes: Two slab pitches on the face just left of the small, deteriorating pocket glacier below the main east-face gully.
Above the slabs, the face forces you left over a small rock wall, then continues straight up through brush/small trees.
Narrows and traverses right ~50 ft along a narrow, jungle-filled ledge with major exposure down the main gully.
Clean rock above the ledge traverse; belay quickly to avoid rope drag (or belay on the ledge).
A further half pitch gains the upper SE ridge.
Scramble around to the right along the upper SE ridge to the summit.

approach: When below the east face, scramble up through brush and easy rock to an obvious slabby rock face just left of the small pocket glacier on the east face.
overview: A committing, brushy Grade IV alpine rock route up Sperry's steep east face, climbing slabby rock beside a shrinking pocket glacier before working through a narrow, exposed jungle ledge and a final ridge scramble to the summit.
beta: Starts with two pitches on the slabby face just left of a small, deteriorating pocket glacier under the large gully on the east face. Above the slab, the face forces you left over a small rock wall, then continues straight up for a couple more pitches through brush and small trees. The route then narrows and traverses right on a narrow, jungle-filled ledge with significant exposure down the main gully; after about 50 ft, when clean rock appears above, head straight up it and belay as soon as possible to avoid rope drag (or belay on the ledge itself). Another half pitch gains the upper SE ridge, from which you scramble around to the right to reach the top. The first-ascent party took 7-8 hours on the route and arrived at the summit after dark, bivying there.
fa: Mike Preiss and M. Bunker, September 24-25, 2002
